claims.statement: For the original fixed selector F(T,p), S(T,p)=Q_p-Q_(p-1), where q_v(j)=i_j(H_v)-i_j(R_v) counts independent j-sets of H_v meeting W_v and Q_j sums q_v(j) over the distinct selected leaf tags. Adjoining v bijects these sets with independent sets containing v whose deletion leaves a set meeting W_v. The stated rooted-component product recurrence is exact. The pinned bounded computations cover all labeled trees through order 8 (with no eligible rows) and T_m for m<=8 only; they do not establish the sign of the marked-rank difference generally.
claims.scope: Exact identities for finite ordinary trees with the original fixed F(T,p) and distinct original-leaf tags. Computation is limited to the stated census and T_m boundaries.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: the fixed-selector rank-difference and rooted recurrence identities are correct, and the bounded outputs replay exactly. Clarify that the q_v bijection targets sets containing v and meeting W_v, not every independent set containing v. There remains no bridge from first descent plus strict selector to Q_p<=Q_(p-1), and the bounded census contains no eligible rows; retain the underlying target only as open.

limitations: No proof of the arbitrary-tree marked-rank comparison was established.
The labeled-tree census through order 8 has no eligible rows, and the T_m computation is bounded to m<=8.
No eligible full-sum counterexample was established; no public theorem was imported.
